# Contact Form Email Feature

**Generated by GitHub Copilot on October 18, 2025**

## Overview

Implement email functionality for the contact form in the portfolio website using MailKit, an open-source .NET library for email handling. Since this is a Blazor WebAssembly application that runs entirely in the browser, we need to create a backend service to handle email sending securely.

## Technical Architecture

### Current Limitation
Blazor WebAssembly applications run entirely in the browser and cannot directly access server-side resources like SMTP servers or store sensitive credentials securely. Therefore, we need a backend service to handle email sending.

### Proposed Solution
Implement a hybrid approach using:
1. **Frontend**: Blazor WebAssembly contact form (existing)
2. **Backend**: ASP.NET Core Web API service using MailKit
3. **Email Library**: MailKit for SMTP email sending

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Backend Email Service
Create a new ASP.NET Core Web API project to handle email sending:

```
src/
├── BlazorApp/ (existing frontend)
├── EmailService/ (new backend API)
│   ├── Controllers/
│   │   └── ContactController.cs
│   ├── Services/
│   │   └── EmailService.cs
│   ├── Models/
│   │   └── ContactRequest.cs
│   └── Program.cs
```

### Phase 2: Frontend Integration
Update the Blazor WebAssembly app to communicate with the backend API.

- Mobile (required) 
- Website (optional)
- EnquiryType (required)
- Message (required)

### 3. Backend Email API (`src/EmailService/`)
ASP.NET Core Web API with:
- **ContactController**: REST endpoint for form submissions
- **EmailService**: MailKit integration for SMTP email sending
- **Configuration**: SMTP settings management
- **Validation**: Server-side data validation
- **Security**: CORS configuration, rate limiting

Enhanced form with:

- Error handling and validation messages
- ~~File attachment support~~ *Will be implemented in a future feature*

## Technical Requirements

### Dependencies
- **Frontend**: No additional packages (uses existing HttpClient)
- **Backend**: 
  - `MailKit` - Email sending
  - `MimeKit` - Email message construction
  - `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Cors` - Cross-origin requests

### Configuration
SMTP settings stored in `appsettings.json` (backend):
```json
{
  "SmtpSettings": {
    "Host": "smtp.gmail.com",
    "Port": 587,
    "Username": "your-email@gmail.com", 
    "Password": "app-specific-password",
    "EnableSsl": true,
    "FromEmail": "noreply@baohconsulting.co.uk",
    "FromName": "BAOH Consulting Contact Form"
  }
}
```

### Security Considerations
- SMTP credentials stored securely (environment variables in production)
- CORS policy restricting frontend domain
- Rate limiting to prevent abuse
- Input validation and sanitization
- ~~File upload restrictions (size, type)~~ *Will be implemented in a future feature*

## API Specification

### POST /api/contact
**Request Body:**
```json
{
  "name": "John Doe",
  "email": "john@example.com",
  "mobile": "07928590809",
  "website": "https://example.com",
  "enquiryType": "general",
  "message": "Hello, I'd like to discuss..."
}
```

*Note: Attachments field removed - will be implemented in a future feature*

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Email sent successfully"
}
```

**Error Response:**
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "Validation failed",
  "errors": ["Email is required", "Message is too short"]
}
```

## Email Template

### Subject Line
`New Contact Form Submission - {EnquiryType} from {Name}`

### Email Body (HTML Format)
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <style>
        body { font-family: Arial, sans-serif; line-height: 1.6; }
        .header { background-color: #4E567E; color: white; padding: 20px; }
        .content { padding: 20px; }
        .field { margin-bottom: 15px; }
        .label { font-weight: bold; color: #4E567E; }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <div class="header">
        <h2>New Contact Form Submission</h2>
    </div>
    <div class="content">
        <div class="field">
            <span class="label">Name:</span> {Name}
        </div>
        <div class="field">
            <span class="label">Email:</span> {Email}
        </div>
        <div class="field">
            <span class="label">Mobile:</span> {Mobile}
        </div>
        <div class="field">
            <span class="label">Website:</span> {Website}
        </div>
        <div class="field">
            <span class="label">Enquiry Type:</span> {EnquiryType}
        </div>
        <div class="field">
            <span class="label">Message:</span>
            <p>{Message}</p>
        </div>
        <div class="field">
            <span class="label">Submitted:</span> {DateTime}
        </div>
    </div>
</body>
</html>
```

## Deployment Considerations

### Development
- Backend API runs on different port (e.g., https://localhost:7001)
- Frontend configured to call localhost API
- CORS enabled for localhost origins

### Production
- Both frontend and backend deployed to Azure
- Azure Static Web Apps with Functions backend, or
- Separate App Service for API with Static Web Apps for frontend
- Environment variables for SMTP configuration
- Custom domain configuration for CORS

## Validation Rules

### Frontend Validation
- Name: Required, minimum 2 characters
- Email: Required, valid email format
- Mobile: Required, valid phone format
- Message: Required, minimum 10 characters
- ~~File attachments: Max 5MB per file, specific extensions only~~ *Will be implemented in a future feature*

### Backend Validation
- Duplicate all frontend validations
- Additional security checks
- Email format verification
- Content sanitization

## Alternative Approaches Considered

1. **Client-side email services** (EmailJS) - Rejected due to security concerns
2. **Azure Communication Services** - More complex setup, higher cost
3. **Third-party form services** (Formspree) - Less control, dependency on external service
4. **Azure Functions** - Could be future enhancement for serverless approach
